findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint instead of keeping it private within the VPC. Combined with the well-known 'admin' master username and an unencrypted transport path, this greatly expands attack surface for credential attacks against the database.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and its snapshots, so all database data is written in cleartext at the storage layer.

findings.issue_category: master credentials in config and state
findings.description: The master username is hard-coded to the predictable value 'admin' and the password is passed via var.password, which is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and reused verbatim in the EC2 user data rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or RDS managed master passwords.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections; the PHP application connects with mysqli_connect without TLS, sending credentials and query data in cleartext.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and password in cleartext and writes them to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF in the hosted PHP app, and is also stored in cleartext in Terraform state and visible in the EC2 console.

The inline policy attached to the EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Compromise of the internet-facing PHP web server yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege-escalation paths such as launching instances with other roles (iam:PassRole aside, ec2:* plus rds:* enables broad data access and snapshot exfiltration).

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is specified, so IMDSv1 remains available. Given the internet-facing PHP application and the account-wide instance profile, an SSRF flaw would allow trivial theft of the role's temporary credentials.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the root volume - which stores the cleartext dbinfo.inc credential file and application data - relies on account defaults and may be unencrypted at rest.
The RDS security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.
